one_line_contribution: That retrieved-experience memory and GEPA-optimized instructions are the same kind of device — inference-time distribution-concentrators that buy pass@1 by deleting reachable solutions rather than adding new ones — and that because they concentrate onto *different* modes, stacking them compounds the coverage loss while sub-adding the pass@1 gain, so the complementarity is only harvestable by splitting conditioning across rollouts (P1) rather than across prompt slots.
closest_prior_work: The proposal names arXiv 2605.28224 as a partial collision and handles it honestly, but the work that most threatens novelty is the one it never cites: the pass@k-boundary literature on RLVR (Yue et al. 2025, 'Does RL Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity Beyond the Base Model?'), together with Large Language Monkeys (2407.21787) and the sharpening formalization (Huang et al., 2412.01951). Those papers *invented* the exact instrument this proposal presents as its contribution — per-instance solve-probability pools, unbiased pass@k, solve-set nesting, and the sharpening-vs-new-capability adjudication — and used it to show that a pass@1-improving intervention narrows the solve set. Coverage accounting is therefore a standard instrument here, and porting it from weight-space to context-conditioning is a transfer, not a new measurement idea; the proposal's framing of 'the coverage accounting' as its own novel contribution (Related Work cluster 4, 'none establishes the training-free, inference-time analogue') overstates the gap, since 2412.10684 already reported retrieval degrading self-consistency and 2505.16067 already gave the mechanism (experience-following). What genuinely survives is narrow: the optimizer-side replication plus the JSD mode-identity test (Prediction 6). That is a real increment, but it is one figure's worth, and it rests entirely on GEPA clearing precheck P-b, which the proposal's own Risk 6 flags as doubtful on an 8B agent.
strongest_objection: The headline concentration result is largely guaranteed by the design, and the one arm that would adjudicate the mechanism is confounded. Three compounding problems. (1) Precheck P-a selects the bank on exactly the axis the hypothesis is about: 'we enrich the bank until it passes' a >=5pt dev pass@1 gain. Among candidate banks, the one maximizing dev pass@1 is the most concentrating one, and its dev-selected >=5pt gain will regress on test — so Prediction 1's 'crossover k* <= 8' becomes easy to satisfy by winner's curse alone, with no coverage destruction required. (2) Risk-mitigation 2 filters the test pool to instances with unconditioned pass@1 in the 30-60% band. That filter deletes precisely the instances where NEW lives (A0 rate near zero), so Prediction 2's 'NEW < 4% of the test set' is partly built in by construction; and it pushes A0's pass@8 toward ceiling, so Prediction 1's 'advantage <= 2 points by k=8' follows from arithmetic compression of a saturating curve rather than from lost coverage. (3) A4, billed as 'the decisive mechanism arm,' cannot decide anything, because temperature-induced diversity is not the same object as conditioning-induced strategy diversity, and matching a scalar summary (mean distinct strategies within 5%) does not match the distribution. If A4 fails to restore pass@8 — the predicted outcome — the result is equally well explained by 'hot sampling produces incoherent, low-quality strategies' as by 'memory shifted the mode.' The falsification path is asymmetric: A4 can kill the mode-shift claim but cannot confirm it. Secondary but checkable: Measurement (e) asserts 'every quantitative prediction above is stated at or beyond' the ~4.5-point MDE. This is false for at least three. Prediction 8 asks for a >=2-point O3-over-O2 pass@1 gap; Prediction 7's sub-additivity margin is 2 points on a three-arm composite whose SE is roughly sqrt(3)x1.7 ~ 3 points; and Prediction 1's k=8 equivalence band is 4 points, where equivalence testing needs more power than superiority, not less. The paper's coupling claim — its declared spine after conceding the memory half to 2605.28224 — is thus stated at effect sizes the design admits it cannot resolve. Finally, on significance: pass@k presumes an oracle verifier, which HotpotQA/MuSiQue agents do not have at deployment. Coverage loss is a diagnostic, not a shipped loss, and the constructive corollary P1 only becomes a method once a selection rule exists; P2 is one arm, not an answer.
what_would_fix_it: Five concrete changes, in order of load. (a) Remove the outcome-axis selection: fix the bank and the GEPA budget by a pre-registered rule that does not condition on pass@1 gain, report the full precheck sweep, and treat bank strength as a measured moderator rather than an entry gate — or, if the gate is kept, use a dev split for selection and a fully disjoint pool for the reported pass@1 delta so the winner's curse is not smuggled into k*. (b) Drop the 30-60% pass@1 instance filter, or report NEW/LOST on the unfiltered pool as the primary and the filtered pool only for curve legibility; as written the filter excises the region where the NEW category can exist. (c) Make A4 two-sided and quality-controlled: also cool A0 down until its diversity matches A1's (does low-diversity A0 lose the same instances?), and add a quality-matched arm (e.g. min-p or best-of-n filtered hot sampling) so a null in A4 cannot be absorbed by 'temperature diversity is bad diversity.' Without this, the mode-shift claim is not testable by A4. (d) Restate Predictions 1, 7 and 8 at effects the design can detect, or raise n per instance for the O-arms specifically — the coupling predictions are the spine and currently sit under the MDE. (e) Add the decoding-diversity portfolio control (below) and commit to a concrete verifier-free selection rule so the portfolio result maps onto a deployment metric. A sixth, cheaper fix: run MIPROv2 on the decisive E1 arms. 'Concentration is the common currency' of prompt optimization is an n=1 claim about GEPA's reflective operator otherwise, and Risk 7 concedes this without repairing it.
missing_baseline: A diversity-only portfolio control: k rollouts of the *unconditioned* agent spread over varied decoding settings and/or paraphrased-but-uninformative instructions (a prompt ensemble), at matched total tokens, run through the identical pass@k pipeline. This is the standard cheap coverage booster, and it is the direct competitor to P1. If mixed-temperature or mixed-paraphrase A0 reaches P1's interior optimum, Prediction 9 shows only that heterogeneity helps — a known result — and nothing about memory and the optimizer occupying complementary modes; the constructive corollary, the paper's payload, then collapses to 'diversify your rollouts.' P1's stated endpoints (A0, A1, O1) do not cover this, because all three are homogeneous-conditioning endpoints. Two lesser omissions a reviewer would also press: (i) a static generic few-shot arm (fixed hand-picked exemplars, token-matched), which is what practitioners actually compare memory against and which A3's off-task decoy does not stand in for — A3 varies relevance, not experience-versus-demonstration; (ii) MIPROv2, acknowledged as cut in Risk 7.
preprint_collision: The check is better than most and should be credited: it names a genuine collision (2605.28224), declines to argue it away, explicitly drops the 'memory reduces diversity' claim, states what survives, discloses that the search budget ran out before three named memory titles and before any OpenReview sweep, and concedes a nontrivial probability that a pass@k-with-and-without-memory figure already exists. That is honest practice. Two things undercut it. First, the unswept region is exactly where the residual claim lives: 'MemCollab, ParamMem, Coarse-to-Fine Grounded Memory' are 2026 memory papers, and a pass@k curve in any of them removes the memory half outright, leaving only the GEPA-coupling half — which Risk 6 concedes may never clear its own precheck. The gap in the search coincides with the load-bearing claim, which is the worst place for it. Second, the check searches only the memory/diversity neighborhood and misses the coverage-accounting neighborhood entirely: Yue et al. 2025 on the RLVR pass@k boundary, Large Language Monkeys (2407.21787), and the sharpening formalization (2412.01951) are not mentioned anywhere in the proposal, yet they own the instrument the proposal advertises as its methodological contribution. A reviewer will read cluster 4's 'none establishes the training-free, inference-time analogue' as a fair statement about the intervention and an unfair one about the measurement. No verdict-changing scoop is demonstrated here, but the claim of an unoccupied methodological gap is not established either.
